prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val][adversarial] Long group header over tiny sub-columns (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Merged cells: "Model" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Benchmark accuracy on he" spans 3 col × 1 row; "Notes" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Model" · longest unbreakable word 39px · one-line width 39px
  col 2: header "Benchmark accuracy on held-out multilingual evaluation suite › EN" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 18px
  col 3: header "Benchmark accuracy on held-out multilingual evaluation suite › ZH" · longest unbreakable word 19px · one-line width 19px
  col 4: header "Benchmark accuracy on held-out multilingual evaluation suite › AR" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 18px
  col 5: header "Notes" · longest unbreakable word 56px · one-line width 514px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 446px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 445px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 446px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Compare benchmark accuracy across three model sizes and three language subsets, with notes providing context for each result.","reading":"Readers scan down each language column to compare model sizes, across each row to compare languages, and then consult the notes for context.","groups":["EN, ZH, and AR are parallel accuracy measures under one shared benchmark header; equal widths support comparison.","Model identifies each row, while Notes supplies supporting prose for that row."],"keep_intact":["Model names","Language identifiers EN, ZH, and AR","Individual accuracy values","Words in the benchmark header and notes"],"may_wrap":["The shared benchmark header can wrap between words across the three metric columns.","Notes can wrap naturally; their row heights can also accommodate any wrapping elsewhere in the row."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[60,55,55,55,220],"idea":"Balance compact, equal metric columns with a generous notes column, while allowing the shared header to wrap."},{"name":"B","widths":[65,70,70,70,170],"idea":"Give the benchmark group more width so its header reads more comfortably, accepting taller notes."},{"name":"C","widths":[60,45,45,45,250],"idea":"Keep the numeric columns just wide enough for their short labels and values, giving notes the most room and letting the shared header wrap more deeply."}]}
